title: Multiclass Boundary Refinement with Neural Cellular Automata for Remote Sensing Land Cover Segmentation

problem.summary: Semantic segmentation of remote sensing imagery often places class boundaries a few pixels away from where they truly lie, and this position error is concentrated in the thin band measured by Boundary IoU (BIoU).
statements: Semantic segmentation of remote sensing imagery often places class boundaries a few pixels away from where they truly lie, and this position error is concentrated in the thin band measured by Boundary IoU (BIoU).

We treat boundary refinement as the iterated application of a small learned local rule: the Boundary Refinement Neural Cellular Automaton (BRNCA), that starts from the class probabilities of a frozen, pre-trained segmenter and corrects them cell by cell.
We generalise the binary rNCA to the multiclass case by keeping the visible channels on the probability simplex through an Aitchison (log-space) update and by adding free hidden channels.

solution.summary: A semantic error assigns a whole region to the wrong class.
solution.approach: A semantic error assigns a whole region to the wrong class.
components: A position error occurs when the interiors of two neighbouring regions are classified correctly but the decision boundary separating them is displaced with respect to the true one.
Global metrics such as IoU mix both effects and are dominated by interiors.

Boundary IoU (BIoU) [3] restricts the computation to a narrow band around the annotated boundary and therefore isolates position error; its complement, Interior IoU (IIoU), measures the remainder of each region.

experiments.summary: First, the contours of natural classes (vegetation, rock, water) are highly irregular and can be characterised by fractal dimension [9, 19].
